rice husk modified by tartaric and citric acids have been shown to be efficient sorbents for the removal of heavy metals from aqueous solutions and the uptake of Cu and Pb increased with the concentration of the modifier, the agitation rate and the decrease in particle size of the sorbent.

tartaric-modified rice husk is an excellent sorbent material for the removal of heavy metals from aqueous solutions and that the sorption capacity is dependent on the pH, temperature, particle size, competitive cations and the presence of chelating agents.

the modified rice husks are good adsorbents for Cu and Pb removal from aqueous solutions and that the uptake of the metal ions is pH and agitation dependent, rapid, exothermic and can be described by the Langmuir model.

the modification of rice hull by carboxylic acid to improve its metal binding capacity.
the removal of metal ions from aqueous solution using a novel sorbent, TARH.

the modified rice husks have the potential for use in wastewater treatment and for recovery of heavy metals from industrial wastewaters.

rice husk, which is a waste byproduct from the rice milling process, can be modified by carboxylic acid and can be used to remove heavy metal ions from aqueous solution.
the modified rice husks are excellent biosorbents for heavy metal removal and that they are environmentally benign, renewable, inexpensive, and readily available.
